opinions.rationale: Searched the 1,376-record screened corpus rather than answering from memory. The emulation-specific half of the entry survives. Mediation terms ANDed with cloning, artificial censoring or censoring weights return four records, and none of them is a method: two are applied emulations that use clone-censor-weight and mention mediation in passing, one is a drug-wide screen, one is a 2013 collider-stratification example. Mediation ANDed with sustained or dynamic strategies or grace periods returns two records, both applied. The phrase proportion mediated returns zero records in the whole screened corpus, so the applied instances the entry cites sit outside the methodological literature entirely, which is consistent with the entry's point that the reporting practice has outrun the estimand. Nothing in the corpus proposes an intermediate variable as a protocol component. The caveat is that the entry frames the estimand problem as a conflict between two families, natural effects needing a cross-world condition and interventional effects failing the sharp mediational null, and a third family exists in the corpus and was constructed for exactly that dilemma. Separable effects decompose the treatment rather than intervene on the mediator, and were defined for a longitudinal mediator with a survival outcome in 2018, generalized to time-varying structures with weaker identification conditions in 2021, and given g-formula identification conditions for longitudinal mediation in 2024. A reader given the entry as written would not learn that the escape route exists. The general-methods half of the entry is also weaker than the corpus supports: the mediational g-formula for time-varying exposures, mediators and confounders sits in the corpus from 2016 and 2017 with a parametric algorithm and released software, which the entry acknowledges in its rationale but its statement does not.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: No mediated estimand is defined for a sustained treatment strategy realized by cloning and artificial censoring, no protocol component holds the mediator, and applied emulations report a proportion mediated on a hazard scale that matches none of the estimands the identification results cover. Three estimand families are available for the general longitudinal case rather than two, since separable effects avoid the cross-world condition by decomposing the treatment, and none of the three has been carried to a cloned and artificially censored design.

counter_evidence.quote: In the context of causal mediation analysis, prevailing notions of direct and indirect effects are based on nested counterfactuals. These can be problematic regarding interpretation and identifiability especially when the mediator is a time-dependent process and the outcome is survival or, more generally, a time-to-event outcome. We propose and discuss an alternative definition of mediated effects that does not suffer from these problems, and is more transparent than the current alternatives.

We propose and discuss a definition of separable effects that is applicable to general time-varying structures, where the separable effects can still be meaningfully interpreted as effects of modified treatments, even when they cannot be regarded as direct and indirect effects. For these settings we derive weaker conditions for identification of separable effects in studies where decomposed, or otherwise modified, treatments are not yet available

we propose a causal interpretation of these two classes of models based on a novel type of causal effects called separable, which overcome some of the issues of natural effects. METHODS: We formally derive conditions for the identifiability of separable mediational effects and their analytical expressions based on the g-formula.

When there are time-varying confounders affected by prior exposure and mediator, natural direct and indirect effects are not identified. However, we define a randomized interventional analogue of natural direct and indirect effects that are identified in this setting. The formula that identifies these effects we refer to as the "mediational g-formula."

opinions.rationale: Searched the 1,376-record screened corpus. The headline claim holds: no record supplies the discrepancy between what an emulation estimates and what a trial estimates, and no record states a criterion for admitting an emulation into a network. The 2022 rheumatoid arthritis synthesis the entry cites is the only record in the corpus that enters emulated trials into a network with randomized trials, and it enters them at face value, so the practice the entry describes is real and unaccompanied by an admission rule. The caveat is on one sentence rather than on the entry. The entry asserts that the estimands differ before any weight is applied and that nothing aligns the two before pooling. For the external and hybrid control route that sentence is refuted by named work in the corpus. A 2024 paper crosses the five estimand-framework attributes with the seven target trial components specifically for external comparator studies and identifies the overlaps and omissions; a second 2024 paper applies both frameworks to an external control analysis in solid tumors as a worked case; a 2025 paper takes the further step of estimating per-protocol effects in external comparator analyses precisely because the intention-to-treat target is hard to interpret when adherence differs between the trial and the external arm, which is the mismatch the entry names. The alignment machinery exists for that route and is recent, so the sentence should be scoped to the network and economic-model routes, where the corpus contains nothing comparable. One scope limitation on this check: power prior, dynamic borrowing and commensurate prior together match one record out of 1,376, so the borrowing literature the entry cites lies almost entirely outside a corpus harvested on target trial phrases, and nothing here confirms or refutes the entry's claims about it.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: An emulation entering a synthesis with randomized trials requires a systematic difference between what the two designs estimate, no method identifies it from the data being combined, and no criterion decides whether a given emulation is exchangeable enough to enter a network. Estimand alignment before pooling has been worked out for the external comparator route since 2024, including per-protocol targets, and remains unaddressed for entry into a network meta-analysis and for substitution into an economic model.

counter_evidence.quote: We offer considerations about the joint application of both frameworks by combining the five EF attributes- treatment, population, endpoint, intercurrent events, and population-level summary-with the seven TTEF components- eligibility criteria, treatment strategies, assignment procedures, follow-up period, outcomes, causal contrasts, and data analysis plan. Any overlap is identified, as well as omissions and unique contributions from both frameworks.

However, the intention-to-treat effect, which is a common target of estimation in ECA studies, is difficult to interpret when there are differences in adherence between the trial and ECA. This paper describes an approach to estimation of per-protocol effects in ECA studies using the target trial emulation framework for study design and analysis based on the results from an exploratory case study (TBASEL).

The estimand attributes of the ideal trial were defined using the estimand framework. The target trial framework was used to address specific issues in defining the estimand attributes using observational data from a nationwide electronic health record-derived de-identified database.

opinions.rationale: Searched the 1,376-record screened corpus and read two records in full text. The core claim survives: every counterfactual performance measure in the corpus is identified under the same exchangeability and positivity conditions used to fit the model, and no record reports how those measures behave when the conditions fail, so the check aimed at the failure mode has no established operating characteristics. Two caveats, both from records the entry does not cite. First, the entry's closing sentence, that applied prediction work stops at predicted probabilities and defines no action space, is contradicted by a 2021 study in the corpus that estimates individual treatment effects for two direct oral anticoagulants, converts them into treatment recommendations, and evaluates those recommendations with c-for-benefit, absolute risk reduction and an absolute risk difference obtained by trial emulation, reporting how many patients would have been recommended something other than what they received. That is the action-space reporting the entry's proposed direction asks for, published four years before the entry. Second, the entry describes the machine-learned antidepressant rule as scored in a held-out test set of 715,246 patients and 739,980 treatment episodes, and carries no citation for it. Both numbers are real and come from the 2021 Taiwanese study that is one of the four gaps behind this entry, but they are the full analysis cohort and the count of next-step episodes, not the test set: the evaluation ran in a randomly assigned 20 percent of patients. The design description is otherwise exact, since that study does state one target trial with four arms. The uncited numeric claim and the misplaced denominator are the two things a reader could check and find wrong.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Counterfactual performance measures for a prediction under a sustained strategy are identified under the same untestable conditions used to fit the model, and no published work establishes how they behave when those conditions fail, so a counterfactual calibration curve is evidence about fit rather than about the assumption carrying the causal claim. Applied work that maps a learned rule to a decision exists and reports c-for-benefit and how many patients would be reassigned, so the absence is of operating characteristics under assumption failure rather than of decision-oriented reporting.

counter_evidence.quote: Model performance was evaluated by the c-for-benefit statistics, absolute risk reduction (ARR), and absolute risk difference (ARD) by trial emulation. Results: A significant proportion of patients would be recommended a different treatment option than they actually received.
We randomly divided the patients into two sets: 80% in training set and 20% in test set.
A total of 715,246 patients with incident depressive disorders were included in the analysis. Among them, 283,927 patients received a next-step treatment, which led to 739,980 treatment episodes.
